reference_action: OP reports pesticide dust residue persisted despite plain hosing/wiping. Validated fix: gently wipe with one-third lemon juice/two-thirds water, then hose off remaining lemon juice. Plain washing already tried is not a matching new fix; mite treatment is a different target.

sources.reason: Oil-treatment burn prevention, wiping neem and alternative insecticidal soap do not provide the acid-assisted dust-residue removal.
Extensive mite-control regimens include alcohol/soap wiping and rinse, but no lemon/dilute-acid cleaning for persistent dust residue. Different treatment goal, not validated remedy.
Alocasia care and Captain Jacks spray for mites, no residue-cleaning solution.
Opened TikTok discovery page provides spray-treatment description but no full video instructions. Visible advice does not match; unavailable underlying content cannot support definitive miss.
Full care transcript including rinse/soap mite treatment at 19:11 onward, no acid-based removal of dust that survives plain rinsing.

actions.action: Keep oil-treated plant away from light until dry

resolved.reason: Confuses neem oil burn/active mite treatment with persistent garden-dust residue. Additional pesticide is unnecessary, but source includes light and wiping safeguards and no definite severe damage is established.

harmfulness.reason: “Keeping them away from light until they dry” supplies a useful oil-treatment precaution. Additional unspecified pesticides and repotting are unnecessary for the stated residue problem and lack application instructions.

specificity_accuracy.reason: The discussion is about neem-treated leaves that burned, while this owner used garden dust and wants residue removed. “Wipe off” repeats an already unsuccessful basic action and omits the validated cleaning approach.

feasibility.reason: Wiping and temporary relocation are easy. “Insecticidal soap takes them out” gives no application details and the vague Captain Jacks recommendation fails to distinguish the product formulations.
